To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

R24571 induces Ca2+ entry into Ehrlich cells, and that the channel is activated by calmodulin, inhibited by Ca2+, and suppressed by nordihydropuaretic acid, AA, quercetin and dihydroquarcetin, suramin and temperature, and that it is not inhibited by thapsigarin, ATP, and ionomycin.
the calmodulin inhibitor (R24571), at low concentrations, induces Ca2+ entry in Ehrlich cells, which is inhibited by calmodulin inhibitors, AA and its metabolites, and by the suramin.
R24571 activates the calmodulin-dependent Ca(2+) channel in EATC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of the channel by R24571 and its interaction with calmodulin and arachidonic acids, and the termination of Ca2+-entry activation.
the properties of the R24571-induced Ca2+ channel, which is a model of the calmodulin-dependent Ca2+ channel.
the properties of a novel Ca2+ channel, whose activation is not accompanied by the depletion of endoplasmic Ca2+ stores and is induced by a calmidazol derivative, R24571, a calmodulin antagonist.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Ca(2+) channels induced by R 24571 in EATC are highly permeable, and the chain of enzymatic processes is not involved into Ca2+ entry, and that the mutual compensation of the processes with opposite contributions may take place.
the Ca(2+)-induced Ca(2+ release mechanism is not involved in the Ca2+ signal induced by the inhibitor R24571.
Ca2+ entry induced by R245-71 is not a consequence of phospholipases activation and that the mechanism of its induction is not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation of a calmodulin-dependent Ca2+ channel is caused by a calmodul inhibitor and that this activation is accompanied by the activation of calpain, phospholipase C, phospholipases A2, and phosphodiesterases.

the calmodulin inhibitor calmidazolum (R24571), in concentrations that do not suppress calmodulin-dependent enzymes, causes a short-term Ca(2+) entry, which is mediated by a calmoduline-dependent Ca(2+) channel.
the Ca2+ signal induced by calmidazol is not a consequence of the inhibition of Ca2+-dependent phospholipase but is due to the direct interaction of R2457 with calmodulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
R24571 is a tool to study the properties of the calmodulin-Ca2+ channel.

the activation of a Ca2+ channel in Ehrlich cells is not due to a decrease in the Ca2+ concentration of the extracellular medium, but rather is a consequence of the interaction of calmodulin and R24571.
R24571 activates Ca2+ channels in Ehrlich cells, which are permeable for Ca2+ and Mn2+ and are inhibited by suramin and nordihydroguaiaretic acid.
